42999789.resumo: Ferric carboxymaltose (FCM) can cause hypophosphatemia through fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)-associated renal phosphate wasting. Patients who have undergone Roux-en-Y gastric bypass may be particularly vulnerable because calcium and vitamin D homeostasis may already be impaired. We describe two women with previous Roux-en-Y gastric bypass who developed severe symptomatic concurrent hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia after FCM. Both had preexisting mineral vulnerability, and the findings are therefore interpreted as a multifactorial interaction rather than evidence that FCM alone caused the hypocalcemia. The first patient, aged 39 years, received FCM 500 mg weekly for five weeks (cumulative dose approximately 2,500 mg) and developed calcium 5.3 mg/dL and phosphate 0.8 mg/dL, with elevated C-terminal FGF23 and inappropriate urinary phosphate excretion during hypophosphatemia. The second patient, aged 37 years, received FCM 500 mg weekly for two doses (cumulative dose 1,000 mg) and presented approximately seven weeks later with calcium 5.9 mg/dL and a subsequent phosphate nadir of 1.3 mg/dL. Her C-terminal FGF23 was measured during early biochemical recovery and remained elevated; urinary phosphate excretion remained measurable during the hypophosphatemic/repletion period, although interpretation was limited by concurrent treatment. Both required prolonged mineral replacement, and the second patient required multiple admissions and repeated IV calcium. These cases suggest that FCM-associated phosphate disturbance may act as an additional metabolic stressor in post-bariatric patients with reduced calcium and vitamin D reserve, producing a severe combined mineral phenotype rather than isolated hypophosphatemia.

10.64898/2026.11.06.764883.resumo: Methanogenic archaea play crucial roles in sedimentary phosphorus cycling, but their capacity for phosphate biomineralization remains poorly understood. Here we demonstrate that Methanobacterium AMB_03, isolated from a serpentinizing environment, mediates extracellular precipitation of carbonate-substituted hydroxyapatite (HAp) under phosphate-enriched conditions. Comparative genomic analysis of AMB_03 versus non-mineralizing strains (Methanobacterium oryzae, Methanoculleus bourgensis MAB1) shows that AMB_03 encodes polyphosphate kinase 1 (ppk1), enabling polyphosphate synthesis from ATP. In contrast, M. oryzae and MAB1 completely lack ppk1, preventing polyphosphate accumulation. Phylogenomic analysis of 320 Methanobacteriota genomes further shows that complete polyP cycling capacity is present in only ~25% of representatives, placing AMB_03 among a minority of methanogens with this capability. Experimental cultivation across phosphate gradients (0-6 mM) showed HAp early-onset precipitation was preferential at [≥]3 mM. Precipitation was eventually observed at all phosphate concentrations (except P0) by 49 weeks and was associated with extracellular polymeric substance production and localized pH increases of up to 8.08. Raman spectroscopy confirmed carbonate-substituted HAp, with characteristic peaks at 960.5 cm-1 (PO43-) and 1070-1072 cm-1 (CO32-). These findings identify a strong genomic association between polyphosphate metabolism genes and biomineralization capacity, suggesting that methanogens with complete polyP cycling systems may create localized phosphate-rich environments that promote authigenic mineral formation in sedimentary systems.

43007036.resumo:
To evaluate how surfactant-mediated biofilm disruption by hops beta (β)-acids extract influences stannous fluoride (SnF2) penetration and interaction with extracellular metabolites, including lipopolysaccharide (LPS).
In two studies, oral biofilms were formed in vivo on artificial enamel surfaces mounted in dental appliances worn by volunteers and subsequently treated ex vivo under controlled conditions. Across the studies, biofilms were treated with supernatants of various commercial 0.454% SnF2 dentifrices containing: (1) pyrophosphate; (2) potassium nitrate (KNO3) and pyrophosphate; (3) tripolyphosphate; and (4) gluconate/citrate-stabilized 0.454% SnF2 (Crest) with and without hops β-acids extract (Activ Bio-Cleanser™). Both studies used phosphate-buffered saline as a negative control (NC). Confocal laser scanning microscopy with component-specific fluorescent probes was used to quantify Sn and LPS distribution relative to bacterial biomass, biofilm thickness, and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) structure. Image analysis was used to quantify Sn and LPS signal within bacterial regions, normalized to bacterial volume or area; statistical comparisons were made across conditions.
SnF2 uptake and penetration varied significantly across formulations. In study 1, the rank order from greatest to least for Sn deposition and LPS neutralization was: gluconate/citrate > KNO3 + pyro > pyro > NC (P < 0.05 between groups). In study 2, the rank order from greatest to least was: gluconate/citrate + hops > gluconate/citrate > tripolyphosphate and KNO3 + pyro > NC (P < 0.05 between groups). Some stabilized SnF2 systems exhibited limited penetration, consistent with diffusion barriers imposed by dense EPS matrices or over-stabilization reducing bioavailability. Gluconate/ citrate-stabilized SnF2-only treated biofilms showed higher deposition per unit bacteria than other SnF2 technologies but uniformly exhibited the majority of uptake in surface regions. In the formulation containing both hops and SnF2, increased Sn penetration and reduced detectable biofilm-associated LPS was observed, consistent with enhanced access of SnF2 to extracellular plaque components following surfactant-enabled biofilm modification. In this case, Sn penetration achieved high relative deposition per unit bacteria in the treated regions throughout the biofilm.
Hops β-acids extract acts as a co-surfactant in toothpaste, capable of modifying EPS structure to improve accessibility and interaction of SnF2 with extracellular metabolites within oral biofilms. The observed changes in Sn penetration and biofilm-associated, extracellular LPS are consistent with enhanced cleaning with reduced concentration of known tissue irritants.
These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for formulation strategies that enhance SnF2 accessibility within adherent oral biofilms through surfactant-based modification of EPS supporting more efficient biofilm management during oral hygiene and providing a basis for selecting toothpastes based on their efficacy.

43005284.resumo:
The development of Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites in the mosquito, Anopheles, is essential for malaria transmission. Despite the unsurprising fact that the mosquito microbiota has become a major factor in the modulation of the competence of mosquitoes, the specific types of microbial taxa and mechanisms affecting the development of the sporozoite are not well synthesized. This systematic review brings together and critically evaluates the available evidence to understand the role of microbiota in the development of P. falciparum sporozoites in Anopheles mosquitoes with a specific focus on the salivary gland microbiome.
A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases (2000-2026) was conducted, and 41 studies met the inclusion criteria. Extraction and synthesis of data were conducted in the form of a narrative in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE's tool for animal studies.
The Wolbachia effects varied by strain and species: wAlbB caused a 3.4- to 3.7-fold decrease in sporozoites, wAnga-Mali had a negative correlation with 95% presence, and there was no correlation for wAnmo in An. moucheti. All African countries (1-57% prevalence) were consistently affected by Microsporidia MB, with no fitness costs. Serratia ureilytica Su_YN1 inhibited ~98% of parasites using outer membrane vesicles loaded with AmLip, which targets parasites via the phosphatidylcholine scavenging pathway. 93% transmission blocking was obtained in mouse models with engineered symbionts (transgenesis + paratransgenesis).
The mosquito microbiota plays a significant, but strain-, species-, and context-dependent role in the development of P. falciparum sporozoites. The Microsporidia and Serratia species are promising candidates for field deployment, offering sustainable, environmentally friendly complements to chemical insecticides for malaria vector control.

42999527.resumo: Malaria remains a leading cause of childhood morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, with severe malarial anemia (SMA; hemoglobin (Hb) < 6.0 g/dL) representing one of the life-threatening complications of Plasmodium falciparum infection. While limited studies have examined host transcriptional responses in SMA, parasite transcriptional adaptations remain unexplored. Here, we performed parasite transcriptomic profiling in the same cohort of Kenyan children under five years of age in whom we previously characterized host transcriptional responses to SMA, including children presenting with SMA (n = 20) or non-SMA malaria (n = 40). Differential expression analysis identified 566 P. falciparum genes associated with SMA, predominantly involving up-regulated transcripts linked to proteostasis, translational regulation, stress-response pathways, and metabolic remodeling. Transcriptomic deconvolution indicated greater trophozoite and schizont representation in SMA, with reduced ring-stage and gametocyte signatures. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and protein-protein interaction network analysis identified coordinated transcriptional programs enriched for proteasomal degradation, ubiquitin-mediated protein turnover, chaperone activity, RNA processing, and metabolic adaptation. XGBoost-SHAP modeling identified a small subset of parasite genes that captured much of the transcriptomic signal, classifying SMA from non-SMA malaria. Collectively, these findings define a distinct parasite transcriptional landscape in SMA characterized by coordinated stress adaptation and metabolic flexibility, highlighting proteostasis-associated pathways for further therapeutic investigation.

43004342.resumo:
Malaria is a vector-borne disease caused by a protozoan parasite in the genus Plasmodium. The parasite is transmitted by female mosquitoes in the genus Anopheles. The disease is common within the tropics, especially in sub-Saharan Africa. The major early clinical features are fever accompanied by headache, joint pains, malaise, vomiting, and diarrhoea. These symptoms are some instances used as a diagnosis for malaria infection without confirmatory laboratory tests; followed by prescription of first-line antimalarials, mainly artemisinin combination therapy (ACTs). This trend of prescribing antimalarials to patients presenting with malaria-like symptoms without confirmatory laboratory tests is contrary to World Health Organization's (WHO) recommended guidelines. Such practices pose a great risk for suboptimal medication, development of resistance against the drugs, treatment failure, and increased morbidity and mortality. Therefore, this study was conducted to evaluate adherence to WHO-recommended guidelines for prescription of ACTs and artesunate.
This was a cross-sectional study in four health facilities in Kilifi County for a period of one year. 9,940 participants consented to inclusion in the survey. Pre- and post-ACTs/artesunate prescription data was captured using standardized case record forms.
Out of the 9,940 patients, 80.4% had confirmed malaria infections, out of which 60% (n = 4,795) were males. 48% (n = 3,836), of the malaria cases were from rural areas. 17% (n = 1,359), of the positive cases were severe malaria, with 92% (n = 1,251), being in children under the age of 15 years old. Adherence to WHO guidelines for diagnosis of malaria was, at 99% (9,841/9,940), with Rapid diagnostic test as the most used technique, at 74% (n = 7,356). Adherence to WHO guidelines for prescription of ACTs was, at 48% (3,184/6,633), with Coartem as the most prescribed ACT, at 98% (n = 6,436). Adherence to WHO guidelines for prescription and administration of artesunate was, at 82% (1,114/1,359). Artesunate injection was administered to all cases of severe malaria.
Adherence to WHO guidelines for prescription of ACTs and artesunate in Kilifi County had improved substantially, although there exists a room for improvement, especially on instructions on how to take the ACT medications following hospital discharge. Therefore, stakeholders, especially the county's ministry of health, should put more effort into further improvement through seminars, short training courses, and workshops to reduce the disease burden and prevent the likelihood of the development of ACTs and artesunate resistance by malaria parasites in the region.

10.64898/2026.11.06.765005.resumo: Malaria remains a leading cause of child mortality in developing countries, with roughly 610,000 deaths per year. While the disease is caused by five human Plasmodium species, Plasmodium falciparum (Pf ) causes the most severe form. Progression from uncomplicated to severe malaria is characterized by high proliferation of the parasite, severely affecting children under five years old. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression remain an active area of research. Many multicopy genes have been implicated in Pf virulence. Some of these genes are implicated in cytoadherence, host-cell invasion, immune evasion, sequestration of infected erythrocytes, and antigenic variation. We employed an integrative transcriptomic analysis in this study to elucidate the molecular underpinnings of severe malaria and gene expression patterns, virulence gene dynamics, and the potential contribution of alternative splicing. Results show an overexpression of protein synthesis and ribosomal genes associated with severe malaria. About 86% (n=1865) of all differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were downregulated in severe malaria, and 226 genes exhibited both differential expression and differential exon usage (DEU). Pf virulence genes and antigenic genes such as var (pfEMP1), stevor, surfin, rif (rifin), ptm-2TM, and msp were upregulated in severe malaria compared with uncomplicated malaria, except for rifin. In severe malaria, there was evidence of co-expression and regulation within multigene families, as well as DEU and alternative splicing in virulence genes and antimalarial resistance-related proteins. Pf does not employ a single mechanism for disease progression but suppresses and deregulates nonessential pathways, processes, and genes, which are upregulated virulence genes, DNA replication, mRNA transcription, and protein synthesis. Multicopy genes are co-expressed and regulated to meet the molecular needs of the parasite. The parasite employs alternative splicing and DEU mechanisms for immune invasion and evasion, host-parasite interaction, as well as antimalarial resistance.

Malaria is one of vector-borne diseases caused by plasmodium species. Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax have a higher prevalence in Ethiopia. To combat this illness, effective therapy is necessary. Chloroquine plus radical cure with 14 days primaquine is a first-line antimalarial treatment for P.vivax. The purpose of this study was to determine the therapeutic efficacy of chloroquine with radical cure with 14 days of primaquine in the treatment of uncomplicated P. vivax in Shecha Health Center, South Ethiopia.
A single-arm, prospective therapeutic efficacy trial was conducted from December 2022 to March 2023 at Shecha Health Center in south Ethiopia. The study subjects were chosen using the purposive sampling technique. The study patients were given a 25 mg/kg standard dosage of chloroquine for three days and a 0.25 mg/kg standard dose of Primaquine for fourteen days. The World Health Organization double-entry Excel sheet was utilized for Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and the laboratory and clinical data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for Social Sciences version-26 software. P-values less than 0.05 were considered statistically significant. The study endpoint was adequate clinical and parasitological response on day 42.
Out of the 100 study participants, 90 (90.0%) completed the 42-day follow-up period. Male research participants make 57 (57%) of the total. Adults made up the majority of the study subjects 60 (60.0%). The adequate clinical and parasitological response rate was 96.7% (95% CI: 90.1-98.9%). On day three, parasitemia was cleared at 80 (82.5%) and fever at 95 (97.9%). There were no serious adverse reactions reported.
Chloroquine plus primaquine is still an effective drug therapy for uncomplicated P.vivax, with rapid clearance of parasitemia, fever, improvement of hemoglobin, and clinical resolution. Therefore, chloroquine plus primaquine should continue as a first-line drug to treat uncomplicated P.vivax malaria in the study area.

Childhood anemia remains a major public health challenge in low- and middle income countries, impairing growth, cognition, and child survival. In Tanzania, the burden remains persistently high, yet its spatial patterns, temporal trends, and links to infectious diseases, particularly malaria, are not well understood.
Using four rounds of the Tanzania Demographic and Health Survey (2007/08-2022) and a Bayesian spatio-temporal geostatistical framework with survey-weighted causal inference, we mapped anemia prevalence and quantified the impact of malaria through estimates of average causal effects (ACE), attributable fractions (AF), and numbers needed to treat (NNT).

Malaria emerged as the strongest predictor of anemia, and its effect strengthened with child age: the odds ratio increased from 2.89 (95% CrI: 2.25-3.72) among children aged 6-23 months to 4.07 (3.53-4.71) among those aged 42-59 months. The ACE of malaria peaked at 0.266 in 2015/16, with an AF of 6.4% and the lowest NNT (3.93) recorded in the same year, indicating malaria prevention was most efficient during this period. Minimum temperature above approximately 18°C was associated with increased anemia risk, while precipitation showed no credible association once malaria status was already accounted for; anemia risk was lower at mid-range cluster altitudes (~1,000-1,600 m), consistent with reduced malaria transmission at these elevations. Lower maternal education, household poverty, larger household size, and younger maternal age were also associated with higher anemia risk.
These findings indicate that childhood anemia in Tanzania is driven by entrenched spatial heterogeneity and a strong, age-dependent, time-varying causal relationship with malaria, highlighting the need for geographically targeted, multisectoral strategies that integrate malaria control with broader social, economic, and environmental interventions.

Imported malaria remains a diagnostic challenge in non-endemic countries, where timely recognition depends on healthcare workers eliciting recent travel history and initiating appropriate testing. We assessed malaria knowledge, training exposure and self-reported travel-history practice across healthcare worker roles at two reference centres in northern Poland.
We conducted an online cross-sectional survey between October 2023 and April 2024 among doctors, nurses, paramedics and allied healthcare personnel. A 25-item instrument covered aetiology, transmission, prevention, pharmacology, diagnosis and epidemiology. Knowledge scores were compared using non-parametric tests. Regression models exploring sociodemographic and occupational predictors were unstable because few respondents scored highly and are reported as supplementary sensitivity analyses.
Among 402 respondents, the mean knowledge score was 7.4 of 25 (29.6%); 91.3% scored below the predefined threshold and no respondent exceeded 64%. Knowledge gaps were greatest for complete transmission routes (4.0% correct), prevention measures (8.7%), diagnostic methods (12.7%) and contemporary pharmacology. Only 14.4% of doctors reported always asking febrile patients about travel to malaria-endemic regions. Malaria exposure in training was limited: 22.1% recalled coverage in parasitology classes and 3.5% had attended relevant symposia or conferences. No sociodemographic or occupational factor was independently associated with knowledge in any model specification.
Preparedness for imported malaria was weak across this non-endemic healthcare workforce. Strengthening case detection requires routine travel-history prompts in febrile-patient assessment, targeted continuing education and structured coverage of imported tropical infections in pre-graduate curricula.

Escalating environmental concerns and widespread resistance to synthetic insecticides have intensified the search for sustainable, plant-based alternatives. Botanical bioinsecticides offer a safer profile for non-target organisms and leave minimal environmental residue while effectively suppressing target vector populations.
Crude extracts from eight native medicinal plants-Ocimum lamiifolium, Lepidium sativum, Amaranthus hybridus, Premna schimperi, Ocimum gratissimum, Argemone mexicana, Lippia adoensis, and Calpurnia aurea-were prepared using 80% methanol and n-hexane solvents. Larvicidal and adulticidal bioassays were conducted under controlled laboratory conditions at concentrations ranging from 62.5 to 2000 ppm against Anopheles arabiensis, Anopheles stephensi, and Aedes aegypti. Mortality data were recorded after 24 h and evaluated via probit analysis to determine LC50 and LC90 values.

Against Anopheles arabiensis larvae, Ocimum gratissimum displayed the highest potency (LC50 = 596.51 ppm; LC90 = 1084.48 ppm), followed closely by Argemone mexicana (LC50 = 650.88 ppm; LC90 = 1039.50 ppm). Against Aedes aegypti larvae, Lippia adoensis yielded an LC50 of 763.03 ppm (LC90 = 1158.01 ppm), while Argemone mexicana yielded an LC50 of 768.00 ppm (LC90 = 995.17 ppm). Notably, Ocimum gratissimum, Argemone mexicana, and Calpurnia aurea induced 100% larval mortality in Anopheles arabiensis at peak ceiling concentrations of 2000 ppm. Furthermore, n-hexane crude extracts of Ocimum lamiifolium, Lepidium sativum, Amaranthus hybridus, Premna schimperi, Argemone mexicana, Lippia adoensis, and Calpurnia aurea exhibited robust adulticidal efficacy against both Anopheles arabiensis and Aedes aegypti across the evaluated concentration spectrum, with Ocimum lamiifolium and Argemone mexicana achieving absolute (100%) adult mortality at 2000 ppm. All 80% methanol extracts produced negligible baseline activity and were excluded from advanced trials.
The non-polar n-hexane fractions of these local plants demonstrate promising baseline laboratory efficacy, highlighting them as candidates for further semi-field evaluation and advanced formulation testing to determine practical viability and payload durability under natural outdoor settings.

43005796.resumo: Critical illness can profoundly disturb the intestinal microbiota-metabolite-host immune axis through the combined effects of shock, hypoxia, altered nutritional intake, antimicrobial exposure, organ dysfunction, and impaired epithelial barrier integrity. These changes can reshape microbial metabolic capacity, host co-metabolism, and systemic metabolite exposure, while the host may simultaneously exhibit overlapping features of hyperinflammation, immune tolerance, lymphocyte dysfunction, impaired antimicrobial defense, and tissue repair. Metabolites generated through microbial metabolism or shared microbial-host pathways may therefore contribute to immune reprogramming, although their effects are highly context dependent and cannot be regarded as uniformly beneficial or detrimental. This narrative review examines short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan-derived indoles, secondary bile acids, succinate, lactate, trimethylamine N-oxide, polyamines, and aromatic metabolites, with particular attention to source attribution, anatomical compartment, host co-metabolism, receptor signaling, and their potential influence on antimicrobial immunity. These metabolites may act through G-protein-coupled receptors, AhR, PXR, FXR, TGR5, VDR, HIF-1α, inflammasome pathways, mitochondrial signaling, and epigenetic mechanisms to modulate macrophages, neutrophils, dendritic cells, innate lymphoid cells, T lymphocytes, epithelial barriers, and endothelial responses. The direction and magnitude of these effects are likely to vary according to timing, concentration, anatomical compartment, immune-cell state, pathogen burden, and renal or hepatic clearance. Within this framework, attenuation of inflammatory signaling may help limit early collateral tissue injury, yet the same response could become disadvantageous when antimicrobial competence is already impaired. Similarly, succinate and lactate may reflect or contribute to distinct inflammatory, regulatory, or reparative programs depending on whether they arise from microbial or host metabolism and whether they act within intracellular or extracellular compartments. Human studies in critically ill populations have linked dysbiosis and metabolomic alterations with secondary infection, prolonged organ support, and mortality; however, most have not been able to resolve microbial source attribution or establish causal mediation. Future work would therefore benefit from integrating longitudinal microbiome, metabolome, immune-function, and organ-clearance measurements with source-resolved approaches, including isotope tracing, as well as state-specific and trajectory-informed clinical endpoints. Notably, pyramided events (DBN3601T and Ruifeng 125) demonstrated higher insecticidal efficacy against resistant larvae than the single-trait DBN9936, particularly in strains with lower resistance levels. Lower transcript levels of ABCC2 and ABCA2 were associated with the resistant phenotypes, but the direct association with the reduced susceptibility was not tested. 42999835.resumo: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is accompanied by extracellular-matrix disruption, metabolic stress and immune-cell infiltration, but how metabolites mediate communication between disc cells and macrophages remains incompletely defined. This narrative review examines lactate, succinate and kynurenine as candidate signalling metabolites at the macrophage-disc cell interface and proposes an integrative metabolite-centred framework. Evidence is strongest for lactate, which is supported by IVDD-specific studies linking glycolytic adaptation and impaired clearance to acidosis, MCT-dependent metabolic coupling, ASIC/NLRP3 activation, lactylation, cellular senescence and matrix catabolism. Evidence for succinate is more limited: IVDD-specific studies support SIRT5-AIFM1-dependent succinylation and mitochondrial dysfunction, whereas succinate accumulation and SUCNR1-mediated macrophage signalling in human degenerative discs remain unverified. The kynurenine-AhR axis is primarily hypothesis-generating; emerging IVDD-related observations implicate AhR and tryptophan-pathway changes, but a causal kynurenine-AhR macrophage-disc pathway has not been established. We propose that degenerating disc cells may reprogramme the local metabolic microenvironment, thereby altering macrophage functional states and creating a self-amplifying immunometabolic loop that feeds back on disc-cell injury and extracellular-matrix degradation. Future studies should combine spatial immunometabolomics in human tissue with cell-specific and causal intervention experiments to distinguish established mechanisms from context-dependent or extrapolated pathways and to evaluate potential microenvironment-directed therapeutic targets.

43005365.resumo: The pore system of coal provides both methane storage sites and migration pathways, controlling coalbed methane (CBM) recovery. In this study, five coal samples ranging from bituminous coal to anthracite were investigated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), low-temperature nitrogen adsorption (LTN2GA), and methane adsorption experiments. The relationships among pore structure parameters, fractal dimension, and methane adsorption behavior were analyzed, and the errors associated with two modified linear methods for calculating Langmuir adsorption constants were evaluated. The results show that highly metamorphosed coals are dominated by micropores and possess larger specific surface areas (SSA). EDS analysis showed that C and O were the dominant elements in the coal samples, accompanied by minor amounts of Al, Si, and S. The fractal dimension exhibits an asymmetric U-shaped trend with decreasing coal rank, and SSA shows an exponential relationship with fractal dimension, particularly within the SSA range of 0-10 m2 g-1. Methane adsorption capacity and adsorption constants increase with decreasing pore size, while pore volume shows no clear correlation with adsorption parameters. Fractal dimension exhibits a positive correlation with adsorption constants, indicating the influence of pore heterogeneity on methane adsorption. The relative errors of adsorption constant a calculated by the two linear methods are 0.08-3.57% and 0.22-1.46%, respectively, while those of b are 0-12.68% and 1.87-16.03%, respectively. The comparison shows that Langmuir parameter estimates depend on the fitting formulation and supports fitting on the original adsorption scale with an appropriate residual model. Although pore characteristics are affected by coal-specific geological conditions, this study provides a useful reference for understanding pore structure-adsorption relationships and CBM reservoir evaluation.

43004734.resumo:
Stroke causes severe neurological damage, blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction, complement activation, and neutrophil infiltration. How complement signaling interacts with infiltrating neutrophils in BBB dysfunction remains unclear.
This study aims to elucidate how the C3a-C3aR axis modulates neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation and thereby contributes to BBB disruption following stroke.
A transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) rat model was used to induce ischemic stroke. Neurological function, infarct volume, and BBB integrity were assessed using behavioral tests, TTC staining, electron microscopy, and BBB permeability assays. Molecular and histological analyses, including RNA sequencing, immunostaining, HE staining, Nissl staining, ELISA, RT-qPCR, Co-IP, and western blotting, were performed to evaluate complement activation, NETs, and inflammatory responses. The C3a-C3aR axis and NETs formation were pharmacologically modulated to determine their roles in post-stroke BBB damage.
BBB damage, neutrophil infiltration, and neurobehavioral deficits are prominent after stroke. On the third day after the stroke, BBB damage is most pronounced. RNA sequencing revealed that inflammatory responses, complement activation, and NETs formation were identified as central mechanisms. Key driver analysis confirmed that C3a-C3aR signaling was associated with neutrophil responses and NETs formation. Increased numbers of neutrophils infiltrated the brain parenchyma and formed NETs after stroke, in association with BBB damage and neurological injury. C3aR was expressed in neutrophils, consistent with a potential role of C3a-C3aR signaling in neutrophil responses. Inhibiting NETs formation mitigated these poor functional outcomes, ameliorating BBB dysfunction. C3a-C3aR signaling was associated with NETs formation and BBB disruption and neurological injury. Suppression of C3a-C3aR signaling reduced NETs formation and was associated with attenuated BBB disruption and neurological impairment. Conversely, activation of C3a-C3aR signaling was associated with increased NETs formation, BBB disruption, and neurological damage.
Thus, our results indicate that C3a-C3aR signaling is associated with NETs formation, BBB damage, and neurological impairment after stroke and may represent a potential target for further investigation.

43004311.resumo:
The effectiveness of long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) depends on both chemical durability and sustained biological efficacy under operational conditions. However, insecticide depletion over time does not always correspond directly to loss of entomological effectiveness. This study assessed the relationship between deltamethrin content and biological efficacy of Yorkool® LLINs over 18 months of household use in Benin.
A longitudinal study was conducted in southern Benin to monitor Yorkool® LLINs at baseline (T0), 7 months (T7), 12 months (T12), and 18 months (T18). Household practice data were collected and analyzed at all time points except T0. However, chemical and biological evaluations were performed only at T0, T12, and T18. Deltamethrin surface concentrations were quantified using a portable C-Vue HPLC device and expressed in mg/m2. Biological efficacy was assessed using WHO cone bioassays with susceptible Anopheles gambiae Kisumu mosquitoes, measuring knock-down at 60 min and mortality at 24 h. Chemical and biological trends were analyzed comparatively.
Mean deltamethrin concentration declined progressively from approximately 55 mg/m2 at T0 to 50.7 mg/m2 at T12 and 45.3 mg/m2 at T18. Despite this chemical depletion, cone bioassays showed consistently high knock-down and mortality rates, with most nets meeting WHO criteria for optimal or minimal effectiveness. The relationship between insecticide concentration and mosquito mortality was positive but non-linear, suggesting a biological threshold effect.
Yorkool® LLINs maintained high biological efficacy during the first 18 months of use despite moderate chemical depletion. These findings suggest that loss of insecticide content does not immediately translate into loss of functional performance. However, the absence of follow-up up to 36 months and the use of a susceptible mosquito strain limit extrapolation to full operational lifespan and resistance settings. Extended durability studies are needed to define the functional failure threshold of LLINs.

Concerning prevention, 45.0% thought that hygiene could help control the disease, but most did not associate this with veterinary health monitoring. Among respondents with dogs, only 5.6% had ever conducted diagnostic tests, all of which were positive. Considering the significance of CVL as a neglected zoonotic disease and public health problem, this study highlights the limited and inconsistent knowledge of the community. The findings emphasize the need for eco-epidemiological surveillance and educational programs targeting dog owners and veterinarians to strengthen control and prevention strategies for leishmaniasis.

10.64898/2026.11.05.764562.resumo: Background. Oropouche virus (OROV) has been reported in areas beyond its historical Amazonian range since 2023, accompanied by rapid growth in publicly available genomic data. However, the extent to which these data provide reliable phylogenetic and epidemiological resolution, and whether that resolution differs among genome segments, has not been systematically examined. Methods. Nucleotide sequences annotated under Orthobunyavirus oropoucheense were retrieved from NCBI Virus (accessed 13 May 2025) and filtered to retain records at least 70% of the reference length for each segment, yielding 898 S, 831 M, and 832 L sequences. Segments were aligned independently with MAFFT, and maximum-likelihood phylogenies were inferred with IQ-TREE using ModelFinder and ultrafast bootstrap approximation. Trees were annotated with collection date, country, and host in iTOL. Results. Phylogenetic resolution differed among segments. Contemporary Brazilian sequences formed a largely unresolved region in the S segment tree, whereas the M and L trees resolved recent clusters to differing degrees. Resolution did not track segment length: the M tree resolved contemporary structure more strongly than the longer L tree, and total tree length was approximately 3.5 times greater in the M tree despite near-identical taxon sampling. Sequences collected before 2010 were recovered in supported clusters in all three segment trees, although their configuration differed by segment. These sequences were also predominantly non-Brazilian and non-human, preventing collection date, geographic origin, and host from being separated as explanations for the observed clustering. The species-level query also retained three reassortant viruses, which may influence segment-specific topologies; sequences annotated to the United States were Iquitos virus rather than OROV. Two Italian sequences clustered with Cuban sequences across all three trees, concordant with published travel histories. Conclusions. Publicly available sequences contain phylogenetic structure that differs among the S, M, and L segment trees, but interpretation is constrained by uneven temporal, geographic, and host sampling and by the inclusion of reassortant species in a species-level dataset. The concentration of sequences from Brazil and human hosts, together with limited representation of non-human hosts, restricts inference about OROV diversity and ecology. Broader and more balanced genomic surveillance would improve the ability to resolve OROV evolutionary and transmission patterns.

42999071.resumo: Most viruses are successful because they can infect and exploit specific host tissues for reproduction and transmission. As a result, we often classify viruses by their ability to infect different tissues: respiratory, reproductive and gut, for example. Thus, knowing the tissue and cellular tropism of a virus may elucidate aspects of its biology including routes of transmission and virulence. We studied tropism of the Drosophila innubila Nudivirus (DiNV) in cells and infected hosts. DiNV is a nudivirus, a family of viruses related to the baculoviruses that are relatively large (150-200 nm), contain large double-stranded DNA genomes, and infect different host tissues. Cultured cells stained with an antibody against the DiNV nucleocapsid demonstrated punctate staining in the cytoplasm by confocal microscopy. Electron micrographs of infected cells, on the other hand demonstrated that virions are present in the nucleus. After purification, DiNV was often associated with multimembrane-like vesicles as described for Oryctes rhinoceros nudivirus. We examined tropism in hosts first by sagittal section and found most virus associated with the gut and, to a lesser extent, reproductive tissues. Upon dissection and electron microscopy, we found that DiNV in the gut is primarily in the visceral muscle of the gut and not the lumen as might be expected for a virus if transmitted fecal-orally.

Sand fly-borne visceral leishmaniasis (VL) has re-emerged in parts of North-central China, while conventional insecticidal control is constrained by the predominantly exophilic ecology of sand flies. Wolbachia-based approaches have shown field utility in medical vector control, but baseline data on Wolbachia infection and strain diversity in sand flies from VL resurgence settings in China remain limited.
Sand flies were collected during 2023-2024 at sentinel sites located in VL resurgence areas across four provincial-level administrative regions in China (Beijing Municipality, Shanxi Province, Henan Province, and Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region). Wolbachia was detected and typed by PCR and sequencing of the Wolbachia surface protein (wsp) gene, followed by estimation of pool positivity and bias-corrected maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)-based individual infection prevalence, haplotype inference, and phylogenetic and haplotype-network analyses.
Three sand fly species-Phlebotomus chinensis, Ph. smirnovi, and Sergentomyia squamirostris-were identified across the surveyed sites. Overall, 268 pools (10 individuals per pool; 2680 specimens) were screened for Wolbachia, and 194 pools were PCR-positive (72.4%). Bias-corrected MLE estimates indicated variable but generally high individual-level Wolbachia prevalence across Phlebotomus sampling sites, ranging from 8.6% to 100.0% in Ph. chinensis and reaching 10.4% in Ph. smirnovi, whereas Se. squamirostris was negative. WSP-based typing resolved eight haplotypes in Wolbachia from the two Phlebotomus species examined, spanning supergroups A and B; notably, Hap4 clustered with cytoplasmic incompatibility-associated Wolbachia lineages (e.g., wPip) reported in mosquitoes.
Wolbachia is highly prevalent in Phlebotomus sand flies from VL resurgence areas in North-central China and exhibits wsp-defined diversity across supergroups A and B. The detection of a wPip-related haplotype (Hap4), together with a locally prevalent Phlebotomus-associated clade, provides a baseline for prioritizing strain-level characterization and functional evaluation of Wolbachia for potential sand fly management in re-emergent VL foci.

43003303.resumo: How microbes and insects influence each other is a topical question in insect science. With this contribution, we highlight joint species distribution models (JSDMs) - which model all microbial taxa in a community jointly rather than one at a time - as a statistical framework particularly well suited for resolving the drivers of host-microbe associations. While JSDM has been widely applied to microbiota of organisms other than insects, only a handful of studies have applied them thus far to insect systems. To encourage insect microbiota researchers to catch up with the benefits of JSDM, we outline the statistical and ecological basics of JSDM and give flesh to the modelling framework by reviewing how it has so far been applied to insect microbiota. We highlight the power of JSDMs in separating host, environmental and microbial drivers of community assembly, and in generating hypotheses about how different microbes influence each other. We further propose a predictive framework for identifying and characterizing five ecological categories of insect-associated microbes: (1) obligate nutritional symbionts; (2) facultative endosymbionts; (3) specialized gut associates; (4) transient microbes; and (5) pathogens and parasites. In particular, we hypothesize how the ecological characteristics of these different microbial categories are reflected in the statistical signatures recovered by JSDMs. We further suggest how JSDM can be applied to address the phylogenetic and ecological scales at which microbiome patterns are structured and to uncover how global environmental changes may reshape insect microbiota.

ensaio.historia:
Durante quase um século, a parasitologia molecular operou sob um dogma redutor: para entender por que um mosquito transmite ou bloqueia a malária, ou por que o camundongo desenvolve edema cerebral, deveríamos buscar sempre "o gene" ou "a citocina". Mapeamos vias inteiras (Toll, Imd, JAK-STAT), sequenciamos transcriptomas de células únicas e quantificamos centenas de RNAs mensageiros.

No entanto, uma pergunta desconfortável permaneceu sem resposta na bancada: **como decisões vitais de infecção ocorrem em frações de segundo, muito antes de qualquer RNA polimerase conseguir transcrever um gene?**

Quando o oocineto atinge o microvilo do mosquito, a digestão do sangue está no auge. Milhões de eritrócitos se rompem, gerando uma pressão coloidosmótica massiva, liberação letal de hemo livre e fluxo turbulento não-newtoniano. O parasito não tem horas para esperar uma via gênica ser ativada. Ele precisa explorar as propriedades biofísicas nativas do epitélio: diferenças de potencial elétrico entre células vizinhas, zonas de menor tensão mecânica e condensação líquida de proteínas de superfície.

Se quisermos descobrir o que não sabemos que existe, precisamos sair da nossa própria vizinhança conceitual. É no cruzamento com a biologia de sistemas de organelas, com a bioeletricidade do desenvolvimento e com a física da matéria mole que residem as próximas grandes viradas da nossa bancada.

grandes_pesquisadores.instituicao: Department of Molecular Genetics, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot, Israel
grandes_pesquisadores.conceito_chave: Contactoma Celular & Comunicação Não-Vesicular de Organelas
grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Maya Schuldiner revolucionou a biologia celular ao quebrar o paradigma de que as organelas intracelulares se comunicavam exclusivamente através de vesículas secretoras (via clássica de Golgi e retículo).

Usando triagem robótica em larga escala de leveduras (SGA - Synthetic Genetic Array) combinada com microscopia de fluorescência de altíssima resolução, seu laboratório no Weizmann descobriu que organelas como retículo endoplasmático, mitocôndrias, peroxissomos, gotas lipídicas e vacúolos estão fisicamente conectadas por pontes proteicas especializadas ("tethers"), formando uma malha contínua chamada de 'contactoma'. Essas fendas de 10 a 30 nanômetros permitem o transporte ultrarrápido de lipídios, íons cálcio e intermediários metabólicos vitais, operando como cabos de alta velocidade dentro da célula.

grandes_pesquisadores.instituicao: Allen Discovery Center, Tufts University & Wyss Institute at Harvard University, USA
grandes_pesquisadores.conceito_chave: Bioeletricidade Morfogenética & Software Biológico de Tecidos
grandes_pesquisadores.historia:
Michael Levin é pioneiro na redefinição da biologia do desenvolvimento e regeneração: enquanto a maioria dos biólogos encara eletricidade celular como algo restrito a neurônios e músculos, Levin provou que **todas as células vivas mantêm gradientes bioelétricos de membrana (Vmem)** e se comunicam através de junções comunicantes (gap junctions).

Seu grupo demonstrou que redes bioelétricas funcionam como um 'software de alto nível' que define a morfologia anatômica, a regeneração de membros e o comportamento inflamatório, conseguindo induzir o crescimento de olhos funcionais em caudas de girinos ou reprogramar tecidos apenas alterando a condutância iônica local.

temas_expansao.o_que_e: Como os gradientes elétricos trans-epiteliais e potenciais de membrana mantêm a ancoragem das junções oclusivas antes de danos estruturais.

temas_expansao.contexto:
O rompimento de junções oclusivas (claudina-5, occludina) tem sido estudado sob a ótica proteica e transcricional. No entanto, pesquisas bioelétricas comprovam que o potencial elétrico trans-epitelial mantém as moléculas de adesão sob tensão mecânica contínua.

tecnicas_emergentes.tecnica: Espectroscopia AFM-IR em Nanoescala (Photo-Thermal Induced Resonance)
tecnicas_emergentes.o_que_e: Combinação de Microscopia de Força Atômica com Espectroscopia de Infravermelho (AFM-IR), permitindo caracterização química de espécies moleculares com resolução espacial de 10 a 20 nanômetros.
tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Durante décadas, a espectroscopia de infravermelho clássica (FTIR) foi limitada pelo limite de difração da luz óptica (~2 a 10 micrômetros), sendo incapaz de identificar compostos químicos dentro de organelas isoladas.

O desenvolvimento do AFM-IR contornou esse limite físico ao utilizar a ponta ultrafina de um microscópio de força atômica para detectar a expansão térmica nanomecânica da amostra quando excitada por um laser infravermelho pulsado e sintonizável. Com isso, tornou-se possível obter o espectro de absorção química exato de nanodomínios lipídicos, agregados amiloides e depósitos minerais sem marcadores fluorescentes.

tecnicas_emergentes.historia:
Por décadas, testar a função de um circuito neuropeptídico ou da motilidade intestinal de um mosquito exigia dissecção traumática, microinjeção de drogas ou silenciamento por RNAi sistêmico (que afeta o inseto por dias).

A criação de canais de rodopsina de canal ativados por luz vermelha (CsChrimson, desenvolvidos por Boyden, Levin e colaboradores) permitiu que pesquisadores ativem subpopulações neurais e células enteroendócrinas específicas com um simples flash de LED vermelho enquanto o inseto voa ou se alimenta em tempo real, sem qualquer agulha ou anestesia.
